judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant turns on whether the policies sit 'excess of underlying insurance which afford limits not less than' the Schedule limits, and 'underlying insurance' is an undefined term whose reach (does a self-insured retention count?) is genuinely arguable; 'written on an occurrence or a claims made basis' adds a second definitional edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article III (c012) expressly contemplates the underlying Hospital Professional Liability limit being 'self-insured', which is hard to square with Article I's requirement of underlying 'insurance', and Amendment No. 4 (c070) substitutes a different first paragraph for later policies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A schedule of dollar figures with defined bases ('each occurrence', 'each medical incident'); little to construe on its face beyond the usual occurrence/incident line-drawing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expanded by Amendment No. 4 (c071, which duplicates the Outpatient Facility entry) and sits against Article III's self-insured HPL exception, giving some cross-document friction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'subject to the provision that a separate Limit of liability may apply in respect thereof' is permissive and unattributed — it does not say who decides or when a separate limit applies, which is a genuine ambiguity about aggregation of limits.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) separately provides that discovery period coverages attaching to ceded policies remain covered, and Rating Schedule-B (c086) promises an extended reporting endorsement 'at no additional cost', so the limit/premium consequences must be harmonised across three places.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare incorporation sentence; nothing in the words themselves is uncertain except which documents are meant.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The attached Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clause No. 2 (c045) breaks off before the Broad Exclusion Provision it incorporates, so what has been 'made a part' is incomplete.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'teaching hospital', 'children's hospital' and 'psychiatric hospital' are undefined categories with fuzzy boundaries, and 'loss arising out of the operation by the insured of' such a hospital is a broad causal phrase capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c053) deletes this exclusion for policies effective on or after July 1, 1995 and narrows it, so which version governs a given loss depends on reconciling the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'total beds' is expressly defined, but the definition mixes 'occupied acute care beds' with unqualified categories, leaving unclear whether occupancy applies throughout.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c054) replaces the 250-bed threshold with 350 beds for later policies, creating a date-dependent inconsistency across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'ownership, operation or use of helicopters owned or leased by the insured hospital' is reasonably concrete, though 'arising out of' is broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c001) affirmatively brings 'Heliport Liability' coverages within the agreement while this exclusion strips out helicopter-related loss, a tension a court could be asked to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of named counties; nothing lexically uncertain except 'covering hospital risks located in'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c055) deletes Cuyahoga County from the exclusion while Rating Schedule-A/B (c061, c081) price Cleveland as Territory 3, so the two versions must be sequenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any pool, syndicate, association, insolvency fund, guaranty fund or other combination of insurers or reinsurers' is a classic enumerated list closed by a catch-all whose reach is uncertain under ejusdem generis.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits comfortably beside exclusion (f) (c010) and the Nuclear Incident pool exclusions (c034, c043); no specific contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'reinsurance assumed by the REINSURED' is a short, well-understood market term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with exclusion (g) (c011) and the Offset article (c032), which contemplates the parties acting as assuming reinsurer or ceding company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'business to the extent that it is reinsured outside of this agreement' uses two vague operators — 'business' and 'to the extent' — and could be read either as an other-insurance mechanism or as a total carve-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Article III's retention scheme (c012/c056/c076) and the Offset article's reference to other reinsurance agreements, but no direct contradiction is evident.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-insured proviso is dense and the figures are internally odd ('$9,000,000 of loss each occurrence/$93,000,000 annual aggregate'), so the arithmetic of the layer can be read more than one way.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This article is deleted and replaced twice (Amendment No. 1, c056, and Amendment No. 4, c076) with different limits, and its 'self-insured' premise sits against Article I's requirement of underlying insurance.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition contains several contestable terms — 90% of extra-contractual and punitive/'compensatory damages awarded to the insured', the condition that the CORPORATION 'counseled with' and 'concurred in' the conduct, and the flat exclusion of claim expenses — each capable of competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be harmonised with Article V's claim-expense indemnity (c017), the exclusions in c016, and the insolvency proviso in the Insolvency Clause (c046), which supplies its own measure of loss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Net salvage, subrogation or any other recovery (after expenses)' is a general catch-all after specifics, and the ordering rule is expressed obliquely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Accounting Schedule (c021) credits to profits 'all salvage received by the CORPORATION', which must be reconciled with this recovery-sharing formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'all payments under the supplementary payments provisions of the REINSURED'S policy, including ... allocated investigation, adjustment, and legal expenses' ties the definition to an external policy form and the word 'allocated' is itself contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because loss expressly excludes claim expenses (c013) while Article V (c017) indemnifies them pro rata, whether expenses erode or sit outside the Article III limits turns on reading all three together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short, concrete carve-outs; 'statutory penalty ... on account of any unfair trade practice' is reasonably determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies both defined terms in c013 and c015 consistently; no conflicting provision located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The pro rata formula ('that proportion of claim expenses ... that the amount of loss ultimately borne by the CORPORATION bears to the total amount of loss') is a perennial source of dispute, and the proviso refers to 'such settlement or appeal' though only an appeal has been mentioned — a dangling antecedent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Article III's limits (c012/c056/c076) and the exclusion of claim expenses from 'loss' (c013), it is genuinely unclear whether expenses are payable in addition to the reinsurance limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A straightforward premium mechanic keyed to an attached schedule and its minimum premiums.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'the Rating Schedule, attached hereto' was deleted and replaced by Schedule-A (c057) and then Schedule-B (c077), so the cross-reference is a moving target.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single-sentence fixed-percentage ceding commission; nothing lexically open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the Accounting Schedule's credit of premium 'net after ceding commission' (c021); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The accounting-period machinery is self-contradictory as written — periods commencing 'January 1st of every other year' running twenty-four months, yet a final period commencing 'the fifth January 1st preceding the termination date' — and the operative first sentence is missing/garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) deletes this first paragraph and substitutes a 40%-of-net-profit formula limited to the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits, which the surviving Accounting Schedule (c021) makes no provision for.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The credit and charge items are mis-numbered and the overhead charge refers to 'Item i of Credits to Profits' without a clean antecedent, leaving the computation open to argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be applied alongside Amendment No. 1's limitation of contingent commission to the first $1,000,000 of reinsured limits (c052), which the schedule never reflects.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'calculated on the reserve of individual cases as developed to the date the computation is made' leaves open whether IBNR and bulk reserves are included — a real and nameable ambiguity in a profit-commission accounting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds the charges in the Accounting Schedule (c021) and the deficit carry-forward (c023); consistent on its face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short arithmetic definition of deficit with a carry-forward rule; little scope for competing readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It mirrors the 'net profit' definition (c024) and the charge items in c021; no inconsistency located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the excess of credits over charges at the end of any accounting period' is a closed formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amendment No. 1 (c052) speaks of 'net profit accruing to the REINSURED', a phrase this definition does not match, which could be argued to change the measure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled and, as far as it can be read, defers all further contingent commission until every premium is earned and every loss paid — an open-ended condition whose trigger is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with the Stipulation of Termination (c099) and the run-off provisions of Article XI (c033) to know when, if ever, a final contingent commission falls due.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Fixed 20-day deadlines and a bordereau 'on a form satisfactory to the CORPORATION'; the satisfaction standard is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the claims-notice duty in Article IX (c027) and the offset right (c032); no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'prompt notice ... of any event or development which might result in a claim' is vague at both ends — 'prompt' and 'might result' — and late-notice fights turn on exactly these words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Insolvency Clause (c047) restates the same duties as surviving insolvency and imposes a 'reasonable time' notice standard, a slightly different measure of the same obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An expressly discretionary participation right ('in the judgment of the CORPORATION'), at the Corporation's own expense; clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside the Reinsured's exclusive control of claims in c027 and the reinsurer's intervention right in the Insolvency Clause (c047) without evident contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'promptly' and 'satisfactory evidence of payment' are soft standards, but the payment trigger is otherwise plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It requires proof of payment before reimbursement whereas the very next paragraph (c030) obliges the Corporation to fund on the day the Reinsured proposes to pay — a sequencing tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is badly mangled and the obligation ('will furnish to the REINSURED the CORPORATION'S payment of loss ... on the date on which the REINSURED proposes to make payment') cannot be applied without supplying words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against c029's requirement of evidence of payment first, so the two reimbursement mechanics have to be reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, permissive, with a plain subject matter ('records ... pertaining to the risks reinsured hereunder').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing elsewhere limits or duplicates the inspection right; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any balance ... under this agreement or under any other reinsurance agreement heretofore or hereafter entered into' is very broad but is drafted as an open, not enumerated, right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Offset rights collide notoriously with the Insolvency Clause's direction of payment to the liquidator (c046), which is the obvious cross-check here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'in no event exceeding 12 months plus odd time' uses the undefined trade phrase 'odd time', and the article shifts between 'terminated' and 'In the event of cancellation' without explanation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Stipulation of Termination (c099) ends the agreement by reference to policies 'issued on or after January 1, 1998', a different cut-off mechanic from this run-off provision, and c025 defers contingent commission past termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard market nuclear pool exclusion, short and categorical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps exclusion (e) of Article II (c009) but does not contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The enumerated installations end with a residual category ('installations other than those listed ... using substantial quantities of radioactive isotopes'), a general-after-specific structure whose reach is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'substantial quantities' is left to the REINSURED as sole judge under c040, which is the only cross-reference and is consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is corrupt in the operative carve-outs and the phrase 'property which is on the same site as a nuclear reactor power plant ... which normally would be insured therewith' is vague as transcribed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to paragraphs (1) and (2) of the same clause (c034, c035) coherently; nothing else in the agreement bears on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'named hazard specifically insured against' is a settled formulation in this standard clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on paragraphs (1)-(3) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As transcribed the sentence is broken ('shall not extend to risks using radioactive isotopes in any form where the nuclear exposure is not considered ... the primary hazard'), and 'primary hazard' is an inherently judgmental test.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The sole-judge provision (c040) is duplicated inside this entry, but there is no conflict with the rest of the agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definition by reference to the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 'or any law amendatory thereof'; determinate in substance though the text is garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the term used in c035 and nothing else; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Making the REINSURED 'sole judge' of 'substantial quantities' and 'the extent of installation, plant or site' expressly hands over two vague standards to one party's judgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the counterpart to c035 and c038 and is duplicated within c038; no contradiction elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A grandfathering rule keyed to fixed dates; the transcription obscures the second date but the mechanic is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 1957/1960 dates are dead letters in a 1994 agreement, which is an oddity of incorporation rather than a genuine conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same grandfathering mechanic for Canadian risks; dates garbled but the structure is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agreement covers US hospital risks by territory (Rating Schedules), so the Canadian provision is inert rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short categorical exclusion of nuclear association membership liability.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Article II(e) (c009) and Nuclear Clause No. 1(1) (c034) without inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Limited Exclusion Provision is set out for classes of personal-lines policies and is heavily garbled, with internal cross-references ('Clause II', 'Clause V') that do not resolve cleanly on the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The personal-lines classes it names (Family Automobile, Homeowners) have nothing to do with the hospital excess liability business described in Article I (c001), so the incorporated form does not fit the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The paragraph announces a 'Broad Exclusion Provision' and then stops — the provision it says the policies shall be deemed to include is simply absent from the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article I (c004) states the Nuclear Incident Exclusion Clauses are 'attached hereto and made a part of this agreement', which cannot be given effect for a clause that is truncated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A standard statutory insolvency clause; the exceptions are enumerated and its judgment-evidence rules are conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It invokes 'Section 4118 of the Insurance Law of New York' in an agreement between Kansas and Ohio companies, and it supplies a measure of 'loss' different from Article IV (c013), which expressly defers to it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'within a reasonable time after such claim is filed' is the only soft standard in an otherwise conventional paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It preserves the Article IX duties (c027) on the liquidator and gives the reinsurer an intervention right parallel to c028; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'a majority in interest' is undefined but is a familiar market phrase, and the apportionment rule is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to expense apportionment 'in accordance with the terms of this reinsurance agreement', i.e. Article V (c017), which is workable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A savings paragraph expressly limited to 'except as hereinabove specifically provided'; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms rather than disturbs the payment rule in c046 and the parties' status under Article III; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The transcription scrambles the lead-in, and 'CRNA's - each full-time equivalent x 5-10' gives a range with no rule for choosing a point within it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This whole Rating Schedule is deleted and replaced by Schedule-A under Amendment No. 1 (c057) and then Schedule-B (c077), while Article VI (c018) still refers to 'the Rating Schedule'.
